subject: Re: Acme POC — eval methodology & success criteria

Subject: Acme POC — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alice / Ben,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on the goals for the POC. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all synced: 

Summary from call:
- Objective: evaluate Redwood inference for Acme’s customer support summarization pipeline (1–2s latency target, under $0.005/token).
- Scope: ~10k weekly requests initially, documents up to 2k tokens.
- Success criteria (high level): accuracy >= 92% on support-summary rubric, end-to-end median latency <= 1.8s, hallucination rate < 3%, and cost within target.

Proposed evaluation plan (details attached):
1) Offline evals (Redwood-run): we’ll run our eval harness on a 500-sample seed set you provide to measure accuracy, hallucination, and cost estimates.
2) Online shadow: 1 week of shadow traffic (no user-visible changes) to validate latency and infra signals in your environment.
3) Grading rubric: combined score across Accuracy / Latency / Hallucination / Cost — proposal attached.

Owners and timeline (proposal):
- Acme: provide seed evaluation set and sample traffic by Fri, 12/04 (Alice / Ben).
- Redwood (Marissa + Dylan): run offline evals and share results by Thu, 12/10.
- Redwood (Engineers/Rachel): stand up shadow infra and start online shadow on Mon, 12/13 for 1 week.
- Joint sync: review results and go/no-go on Mon, 12/20.

Attachments: acme_poc_eval_plan_v1.pdf (POC plan), acme_success_criteria.xlsx (success criteria template).

Please confirm owners/timeline or propose adjustments. Happy to jump on a quick 15-min follow-up if that’s easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Acme POC — eval methodology & rubric proposal

Perfect, thanks Alice — appreciate the precision on metrics. Based on that feedback I’m proposing a slightly more detailed evaluation methodology and a grading rubric so we have an objective go/no-go. Highlights below (full rubric attached):

Proposed methodology (hybrid):
- Offline evals (Redwood-run): run on your 500-sample seed and an additional held-out set (if you have one). Metrics: accuracy (exact/ROUGE-style), precision/recall for extraction, hallucination flag rate, token-level cost estimate.
- Shadow (1 week): monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and business-level degradation signals. We’ll also run a 2-hour stress window on day 2 to observe tail behavior.

Proposed grading rubric (weights):
- Accuracy / Extraction quality: 40% (threshold >= 0.92 weighted score)
- Latency (p95): 25% (target <= 1.8s)
- Hallucination rate: 20% (target < 3%)
- Cost per 1k tokens: 15% (target <= $5 per 1k — adjust based on your budgeting)

Pass threshold: combined weighted score >= 0.80. Any single critical failure (e.g., p95 > 3s or hallucination > 7%) triggers an automatic mitigation plan before go-live.

Next steps I propose:
1) Acme provides seed set + internal criteria by 12/04.
2) Redwood runs offline evals and shares full report by 12/10.
3) Shadow infra ready by 12/12; shadow runs 12/13–12/19 (one week).
4) Joint review on 12/20.

Attachment: eval_rubric_v1.xlsx (grading sheet).

Dylan / Rachel — are these timelines OK on your side? Rachel, can your team stand up the shadow infra and SSO links (we’ll need an ingest endpoint + access logs)?

Thanks — will update the HubSpot deal with timeline and attach the rubric.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
